key_insight: Tensor-network decompositions turn a high-dimensional quantum dynamics problem into independent lower-dimensional propagations that can run in parallel across distributed quantum and classical hardware.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a practical route to hybrid, asynchronous quantum computing for molecular simulation, while also reducing two-qubit gate cost by using native partial-entangling gates.
method: Represent the time-evolution operator as a tensor network in an elevated Hilbert space.
Decompose the coupled dynamics into independent subproblems that can be executed asynchronously on heterogeneous devices.
Compile the distributed circuits on trapped-ion hardware using native XX(θ) entangling gates.
evidence_signal: On a small protonated water cluster, the quantum-computed vibrational spectra matched classical results within 4 cm^-1, and the compiled gate strategy reduced expected two-qubit infidelity by more than 30%.
watch_item: The approach depends on effective tensor-network decomposition and hardware-specific compilation, so performance and scalability may vary across quantum platforms and problem sizes.
paper_title: Tensor-Network-Based Distributed Quantum Dynamics on Independent Quantum Computers
